issues.t: 2.4L engine burns oil (warranty extension)
issues.sym: The oil level drops noticeably between oil changes, the low oil pressure light comes on, or you see bluish smoke and smell burning oil. Left alone it can lead to a ticking or knocking engine.
issues.why: The 2.4L Tigershark engine can let oil slip past the piston rings and burn it. FCA settled a class action over it and extended coverage to 7 years or 100,000 miles on 2015-2018 Renegades built through December 7, 2018 (bulletin 09-003-23). Under that program, a vehicle that fails an oil consumption test gets a new engine long block.
issues.next: Check the dipstick every fill-up or two and top off with the correct oil. Ask a Jeep dealer for an oil consumption test and whether your VIN is still inside the 7-year/100,000-mile extension. Never drive with the oil pressure light on.

issues.t: Rough, jerky or delayed shifting from the 9-speed automatic
issues.sym: Harsh 1-2 and 2-3 shifts, a lurch or bang when slowing down, a hesitation pulling away from a stop, slow engagement out of Park, or the transmission seeming to stick in one gear.
issues.why: The ZF-designed 9-speed automatic relies heavily on software, and early calibrations shifted poorly. Jeep released many transmission computer updates, and a few vehicles needed a valve body or other internal repair.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for and install all transmission software updates and do a shift relearn. If shifting stays harsh or it gets stuck in a gear, have the fluid and codes checked before it causes more wear.

issues.t: Transmission may shift to neutral without warning (recall)
issues.sym: While driving, the transmission suddenly drops into neutral and the vehicle coasts with no power, sometimes with a warning light.
issues.why: Crimped connections in the transmission wiring harness might not make good contact, so the transmission can lose its gear signal and go to neutral.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for recall 16V-529. The dealer reprograms the engine and transmission computers and replaces the range sensor harness if needed, for free.

issues.t: Engine stalls or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off or drops into reduced-power (limp) mode, the gas pedal stops responding, and steering gets heavy after a stall. It can happen at low speed or on the highway.
issues.why: Stalling is the most common engine complaint for 2015-2018 Renegades. Reported causes include a failing electronic throttle body, fuel delivery problems and engine computer software faults, several of which were addressed by recalls and updates.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get off the road safely if it stalls. Have the stored codes read, check your VIN for open recalls, and ask the dealer for any engine computer updates before replacing parts.

issues.t: 4x4 power transfer unit or rear drive unit failure
issues.sym: A whine, growl or rumble that rises with speed, a Service 4WD warning, grinding when coasting or on light throttle, or the 4x4 system shutting itself off.
issues.why: On 4x4 Renegades the power transfer unit (PTU) that sends power to the rear, its actuator, or the rear drive unit can wear out or fail internally. Some early problems were fixed with software updates, others needed new parts.
issues.next: Have a shop pinpoint whether the noise is from the PTU, rear unit or a wheel bearing. Changing the PTU fluid about every 30,000 miles helps prevent damage.

issues.t: Radiator cooling fan fails and engine overheats (notice V54)
issues.sym: A wobbling or noisy fan, the temperature gauge climbing in traffic, a check engine light, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The electric radiator cooling fan on these years has an internal part that can fail early, so the engine is not cooled at low speeds. FCA issued Customer Satisfaction Notification V54 to replace the fan free and reimburse owners who had already paid.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Ask a Jeep dealer whether notice V54 was done on your VIN; if you paid for a fan replacement, keep the receipt.

issues.t: Coolant loss and overheating
issues.sym: The coolant reservoir keeps going low, the temperature gauge rises, a sweet smell inside the cabin, or foggy windows. Some owners also see warning lights after coolant reaches wiring behind the dash.
issues.why: Overheating and coolant loss are among the top engine complaints on 2016 Renegades. Owners report leaks from the thermostat housing and from the heater core behind the dashboard.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up with the correct type and have a pressure test done to find the leak. Do not keep driving with the gauge in the red.

issues.t: Cracked oil pump housing (recall)
issues.sym: The oil pressure warning comes on, the engine gets noisy, or it stalls.
issues.why: The oil pump housing, which is part of the balance shaft module, could be cracked from manufacturing, letting the oil pump fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-131. Turn the engine off right away if the oil pressure warning comes on.

issues.t: Fuel pump may lose pressure and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, loses power or stalls under heavy load, especially in hot weather or at high altitude.
issues.why: A manufacturing error in the fuel pump assembly on some front-wheel-drive flex-fuel Renegades can cause fuel pressure to drop when the engine needs the most fuel.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for recall 18V-731. The dealer replaces the fuel pump free.

issues.t: Engine computer chip failure (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or will not start.
issues.why: A voltage regulator chip inside the powertrain control module can fail.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-524. The dealer replaces the engine computer free.

issues.t: Misfire and rough running from ignition coil boots (TSB)
issues.sym: A check engine light (often flashing), shaking at idle, and a rough or weak engine, with misfire codes P0300-P0304.
issues.why: The rubber boots that connect the ignition coils to the spark plugs can break down and let the spark leak away. Jeep's bulletin 08-027-20 replaces all four boots with an updated kit and special grease.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Ask the shop about bulletin 08-027-20 and check the spark plugs at the same time.

issues.t: Jerking or limp mode with code P2173 (TSB)
issues.sym: The engine jerks, loses power or goes into limp mode, and the check engine light comes on with code P2173.
issues.why: The engine computer sees an air leak in the intake system. Jeep's bulletin 09-010-20 fixes it by installing a modified oil vapor (breather) inlet tube with a small restrictor.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask the shop about bulletin 09-010-20. It is a quick repair.

issues.t: Cranks but won't start in freezing weather (muffler TSB)
issues.sym: On a very cold morning the engine turns over but will not start, then starts normally once it warms up.
issues.why: Some mufflers were built without a small drain hole. Water from normal exhaust condensation collects inside and freezes, blocking the exhaust. Bulletin 09-004-20 has a technician drill a 1/8-inch weep hole.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop to check the muffler for a weep hole. It is a very quick fix.

issues.t: Stop/Start not ready message and battery sensor faults
issues.sym: A Stop/Start Not Ready or battery charging message, the auto stop/start feature quitting (often in winter), slow cranking, or a battery that keeps going flat.
issues.why: The stop/start system watches the battery through an intelligent battery sensor on the negative cable. A weak battery or failed sensor makes the system shut stop/start off, and Jeep issued service guidance for these faults.
issues.next: Have the main battery load-tested first. If it is good, the battery sensor is the usual culprit. Use the correct AGM battery when replacing it.

issues.t: Uconnect screen, Bluetooth and electrical glitches
issues.sym: The radio screen freezes, goes black or reboots, Bluetooth drops, random warning lights appear, door locks act up, or dash lights flicker.
issues.why: Software bugs in the Uconnect radio and body control module cause many of these. Some vehicles needed a new radio unit or body control module.
issues.next: Try a radio reset by holding the power button. Ask the dealer for radio and module software updates, which may be covered under bulletins.

issues.t: Key not detected or push-button no-start
issues.sym: A Key Not Detected message, the push-button start needing several tries, or the engine not starting at all even with the key fob inside.
issues.why: The keyless entry and start system can lose track of the fob because of a weak fob battery, a software fault in the hub module, or a failing start button. Jeep issued service guidance on intermittent no-starts with multiple start attempts.
issues.next: Replace the key fob battery first. If it continues, have the dealer check for module software updates and test the start button.

issues.t: My Sky roof panel leaks, rattles or sticks
issues.sym: Water in the footwells or on the headliner after rain, a musty smell, rattling or creaking from the roof panels, or a power panel that sticks open.
issues.why: The removable My Sky roof panels rely on drain tubes and rubber seals that clog or wear. Loose brackets and clips cause rattles, and Jeep issued bulletins for panels that stick or run roughly.
issues.next: Clear the roof drain tubes and inspect the seals. Dry wet carpet quickly to prevent mold and wiring problems, and ask the dealer about the My Sky bulletins.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from a refrigerant leak
issues.sym: The air conditioning slowly stops cooling or blows warm air.
issues.why: Owners report leaks at the condenser and refrigerant lines. Jeep also issued a bulletin for leaking A/C suction lines with a faulty crimp.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested with dye before recharging, so you are not paying for refrigerant that leaks back out.

issues.t: Squealing brakes and rusty front rotors
issues.sym: Brakes squeal, especially when cold or in reverse, or the front rotors rust, wear unevenly and cause vibration early.
issues.why: Squealing brakes are one of the most reported 2015 Renegade problems. Owners also report front rotors rusting and needing replacement at low miles.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors inspected. Quality pads and coated rotors usually cure it.

issues.t: Creak or rattle from the front suspension (TSB)
issues.sym: A creaking or rattling noise from the front corners over bumps or when turning.
issues.why: The front coil springs can rub and creak at their seats. Jeep issued bulletin 02-009-17 to add a protective sleeve to the springs.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about bulletin 02-009-17, and have the struts and links checked if the noise continues.

issues.t: Trailer hitch may be missing bolts (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. In the worst case, the hitch could loosen or separate while towing.
issues.why: Some factory hitches were fastened with one bolt per side instead of three.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 16V-545 before towing. The dealer adds the missing bolts free.

issues.t: Radio software could allow remote hacking (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms.
issues.why: Weaknesses in the radio software could let an outsider reach other vehicle systems through the network.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 15V-508. The software fix is free from the dealer.

issues.t: Many warning lights come on with no fault (recall)
issues.sym: Several warning lights light up on the dash at once even though nothing is wrong.
issues.why: A software problem in the instrument cluster could turn on warning lamps falsely.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V-485. The dealer updates the cluster software free.

issues.t: Airbag controller software may disable safety systems (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag warning light may come on, or there may be no warning at all.
issues.why: Incorrect software in the occupant restraint controller could switch off airbags and seatbelt tensioners. On some Upland models the controller could also be calibrated wrong.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 19V-287 and 19V-438. The dealer updates or replaces the controller free.

issues.t: Backup camera image stays on after reverse (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture stays on the screen after you shift out of reverse.
issues.why: A radio software error kept the image displayed longer than federal rules allow.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-191. The radio update is free at a dealer or over the air.

issues.t: Rear brake caliper may be cracked (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk or grinding from the rear, a brake fluid leak, or a softer brake pedal.
issues.why: A right rear brake caliper could have been fractured when it was cast.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-909. The dealer inspects and replaces the caliper free.

issues.t: Seat belt buckle sensor may stop the front airbag (recall)
issues.sym: An airbag or seatbelt warning light may come on, or there may be no warning.
issues.why: The connector for the seat belt buckle switch could be loose, which can keep the front seat airbag from deploying correctly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-510. The dealer repairs the connection free.

issues.t: Wrong reverse light assembly installed (recall)
issues.sym: The reverse light in the rear bumper may be dim or hard for other drivers to see.
issues.why: Some vehicles were built with an incorrect bumper reverse light assembly that does not meet the lighting standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-918. The dealer inspects and replaces it free.
